title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1970-10-04
lineage: SBD > FM > MR > Reel > ? > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with minor distortion delivers a high‑energy, short set highlighted by a definitive China > Rider and the rare Till The Morning Comes.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its intensity and tight performances – especially Phil Lesh’s booming bass, Jerry Garcia’s crisp guitar tone, and the celebrated China‑Rider transition.  While the soundboard source is generally clear, listeners note occasional distortion at high volume, a blip on “Casey Jones” and other minor quirks.  Overall the set flows well despite its brevity, offering strong renditions of Cold Rain & Snow, Good Lovin’ (drum solo), Sugar Magnolia and the seldom‑played Till The Morning Comes.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight strong musical moments; recording issues are noted but not severe, leading to an overall rating near 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear mix with slight distortion when turned up loud, Phil's backup vocals a bit high early on, occasional blip on “Casey Jones” and other minor sound quirks.

poor_songs: Brokedown Palace (mixed opinions, some find it weak)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, high‑energy hour that favors quantity over long jams; songs transition smoothly with a strong early burst and maintain momentum despite limited time.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is praised as crisp, snappy, creative and especially notable on the intro to Rider.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh receives abundant praise for booming, sharp bass playing and prominent vocals; his mix is occasionally a bit loud.
band_member_comments.Drums: Good Lovin' drum solo highlighted as awesome; occasional sloppy coordination noted in later songs.
